tagline: I connect people who don't know they need each other.
definition: Heirloom trades: businesses whose worth is handed down rather than scaled up.

towns.name: Hungerford
towns.day: Wednesday market, or the antiques fair on the 2nd Sunday (8 Nov, 13 Dec)
towns.why: Antiques town with 100+ dealers on one High Street. Dreweatts, a major auction house, is 15 minutes away.
towns.travel: Train from Paddington, about 1h05 (some trains change at Reading). Car: M4 J14, about 1h30.
towns.bestDay: Wednesday (charter and indoor market) or the antiques fair on the 2nd Sunday of each month in the Town Hall.
towns.dates: Antiques fair Sun 8 Nov and Sun 13 Dec. Dreweatts Fine Jewellery 18 Nov, Fine Watches 19 Nov.

towns.name: Tetbury
towns.go: Paddington to Kemble, about 1h15, then a taxi
towns.why: The Cotswolds' antiques capital, with top dealers along Long Street, a Bonhams office in town and estate money all around.
towns.travel: Train from Paddington to Kemble, about 1h15, then a 15-minute taxi. Car: M4 J17, about 2h.
towns.bestDay: Wednesday (market day). Pair it with a Moore Allen & Innocent sale day in Cirencester.
towns.dates: Moore Allen & Innocent live sale Thu 5 Nov.

towns.name: Petworth
towns.day: Tuesday to Saturday, when most dealers are in
towns.go: Victoria to Pulborough, about 1h15, then a taxi
towns.why: A small Sussex town packed with fine-antiques dealers, many in the local dealers' association (PAADA), next to the Petworth estate.
towns.travel: Train from Victoria to Pulborough, about 1h15, then a 15-minute taxi. Car: A3 then A283, about 1h45.
towns.bestDay: Tuesday to Saturday, when most dealers are in. The Antiques Market is open 7 days.
towns.dates: Toovey's (20 minutes away) holds regular specialist sales. Check tooveys.com before you go.

towns.name: Lewes
towns.why: A long-running weekly auction (Gorringe's), Cliffe High Street's antiques centres, and 230-year-old Harvey's Brewery.
towns.travel: Direct train from Victoria, about 1h05. Everything is walkable from the station.
towns.bestDay: Monday: Gorringe's weekly sale, with the room full of dealers and executors. Farmers' market 1st and 3rd Saturdays.
towns.dates: Gorringe's Fine Art & Interiors Tue 3 Nov. House & Garden sale Mon 9 Nov.

towns.name: Henley-on-Thames
towns.why: A wealthy riverside town with an auction house, two rare-book dealers, a family jeweller and a boatyard family firm dating from 1870.
towns.travel: Train from Paddington, changing at Twyford, about 1h. Car: M4 J8/9, about 1h15.
towns.dates: Check The Pedestal's sale calendar. Viewing days are the easiest time to chat.

towns.name: Bicester Heritage
towns.go: Marylebone, about 50 min, then a taxi
towns.why: A former RAF base with 50+ classic and supercar specialists, including Broad Arrow (auctions), Hagerty (valuations and insurance) and car-collection managers.
towns.travel: Train from Marylebone to Bicester, about 50 min, then a 5-minute taxi. Car: M40 J9, about 1h15.
towns.bestDay: A Scramble Sunday, when every workshop opens to the public. On other days, book visits ahead.
towns.dates: Scramble Sun 10 Jan 2027, Super Scramble 24–25 Apr 2027, Scramble Sun 3 Oct 2027.

towns.name: Cobham & Weybridge
towns.why: Surrey's supercar belt: Brooklands, a classic-car auction at Mercedes-Benz World, a 1979 family jeweller, and your dealer partner Scuderia Prestige nearby.
towns.travel: Train from Waterloo to Weybridge, about 30 min, or to Cobham & Stoke d'Abernon, about 35 min. Car: A3/M25 J10, about 45 min.
towns.bestDay: Saturday 28 Nov: Historics' Brooklands Velocity sale (viewing 26–27 Nov).
towns.dates: Historics at Mercedes-Benz World Sat 28 Nov.

dealer.label: Antiques dealer
dealer.read: Owner-run, proud of their eye. Often wants to be seen as the expert (intelligence) or recognised for what they've built (significance).
dealer.listen: Where stock comes from (clearances, executors). Who's retiring. Any 'so I can finally…' line.

auction.label: Auctioneer or valuer
auction.read: Relationship-driven and always short of good consignments. Likes being first to know.
auction.listen: Which solicitors refer to them. Coming single-owner sales. Cars or watches in estates they can't handle.

solicitor.label: Probate solicitor
solicitor.read: Careful and reputation-first. Wants reassurance (approval) that anyone they refer is discreet.
solicitor.listen: Kinds of estate they struggle to place (cars, wine, watches). Never ask about clients.

dealerFast.label: Classic car or watch dealer
dealerFast.read: Fast and stock-hungry. Needs cars (or pieces) to sell and buyers who are serious.
dealerFast.listen: Wanted lists that match your supercar leads. Collections about to come up.

founder.label: Family-firm owner
founder.read: Has built something over decades. Often cares about legacy (significance) and peace more than price.
founder.listen: 'The kids aren't interested', 'one day…', 'so I can finally travel' (freedom). Never open with 'Are you selling?'

host.label: Connector or host
host.read: Judged on who they bring together, so being useful to members matters more than any deal (acceptance). Suggestion: not on the source Page.
host.listen: Who's new, who's struggling, which members need an introduction. Events you could help at.

flow.do: Outside: three slow breaths and name the feeling ('nerves, noted'). Walk in at pool speed, hands visible, shoulders down. Aim to be the most comfortable person in the room.
flow.say: Hi, I'm Cyrus. Not buying or selling today, just getting to know the people in town. How long have you been here?

flow.do: Notice their normal pace, volume and posture, then look only for changes. Match their energy for the first minute, then lift gently. Listen for 'I built' (significance) or 'we, our team' (acceptance). If something shifts, ask, don't diagnose.
flow.say: Is now good, or shall I pop back when it's quieter?

flow.do: Warmth first, then competence. Ask two follow-ups before you say anything about yourself. Listen with your face: slow nods, a head tilt. FORD (family, occupation, recreation, dreams) gives you topics.
flow.say: Working on anything exciting? · What do you do in your free time?

flow.do: When they ask what you do, tell the 10-second story. Slow right down on the line that matters, pause after it, and finish on a lower pitch.
flow.say: I connect people who don't know they need each other. (Then pause.)

flow.stage: Getting the contact and coming back
flow.do: End on purpose: mention something in the future, then a compliment or an action. Ask for the card once, calmly, then stop talking. Same day, send a short note. Come back in 4–6 weeks. Three visits before you ask for anything.
flow.say: It's been lovely talking. Good luck with the sale. Could I take a card? I'll pop back next month.

flow.do: Ask each side privately first. Reframe it so neither feels sold to (perception, context, permission). Explain it in their terms, 'so you can finally…'. Only introduce if it's in both people's interest.
flow.say: No pressure and not a sale. I just think you two should know each other. Happy for me to introduce you?
